name: f7-promotion-drive-v1
hypothesis: The weak-review streak is a promotion bottleneck, not a balance problem: no review after the first gave a B at Level 1 (0 of 47), every game still at Level 1 after its third review ended by month 24 (12 of 12), and the first promotion's timing sets the score (promoted at review 1: mean Q 57.3, 12 of 14 completed; at review 2: 47.0, 7 of 11; not by review 2: 22.0, 0 of 13). Balanced play spends quarters on statistics that have stopped rising, and the leader's notes mark most dimensions at risk on most turns. A temporary single priority (P12) - while the latest review did not promote you, take the story option that best shows delivered results or raises standing with decision makers at a bounded cost, with Apply for a key project as main action, and only Health, Dignity, Wealth and risk warnings as exceptions - brings the first promotion earlier than the leader's balanced rules. f8-secure-growth, whose Grow mode played this way before its first review, was promoted at review 1 in 3 of 4 Haiku games against 14 of 38 overall.
change: Leader's three Skills with f8's Grow story preference and key-project main action, gated by a feedback mode. risk-review: 'Promotion drive is on unless your Level rose at the latest review', named in each note. story-decisions: during the drive rule 1 applies only to Health, Dignity and Wealth, and new rule 2 picks the option that best shows delivered results or raises standing with decision makers at a bounded cost over comfortable options, never hiding a problem and closing problems first after strong or repeated risk warnings; outside the drive the parent's rules (merged into one line). quarterly-planning: main action Apply for a key project during the drive, otherwise the parent's weakest-dimension rule; the C/D Report-results clause is dropped (the drive covers non-promoting reviews); Energy unchanged. Shared trims in all three block-3 children (no strategy change): shorter front-matter descriptions with the same 'Use ...' triggers; the redundant line 'Do this before every decision.' removed; the check_latest_logs line shortened to the context-reset case; quarterly step 4 ('Keep the same rules all run; near the end, avoid new risks.') removed because 'near the end' is a run-phase trigger the block-3 brief forbids. Manifest instruction kept identical to the parent's routing sentence (the generic template has an empty instruction; keeping it avoids a routing confound). 389 words by wc -w (parent 398).
learning_goal: Find out whether the bottleneck the traces point to (leaving the starting level; every B after the first review came at Level 2 or above) responds to concentration: does a feedback-gated single priority on delivered results and standing bring the first promotion earlier than the leader's balanced, risk-first rules, and what does it cost in Network, risk warnings and trust crises? A gain would justify a promotion-drive branch for the DeepSeek screen; a loss through collateral damage would show that the leader's balance protects something the reviews need; no change would say the first promotion is mostly outside the policy's reach for Haiku.
predicted_behaviour: Notes name the drive on before the first review and after any review without a promotion, off in the half-year after a promotion, in at least 90% of decisions. Main action Apply for a key project in at least 90% of drive quarters; Lay low only with Health at risk. Story choices in the drive favour delivering or showing results and visible work with decision makers; fewer options chosen for comfort or relationships. First promotion at review 1 in at least 3 of 4 runs (population 14 of 38), ending level at or above the parent's, mean quantitative_score at or above the parent's raw mean (59.7). Expected costs: Network below its high at more reviews than the parent, and more months with the HR remark at 'piled up' or worse.
refutation: On a 4-run Haiku screen against f7-three-skills-v1, refuted (P12 decision rule: collateral damage exceeds progress, or the bottleneck was misidentified) if the first promotion is not earlier on average than the parent's and mean quantitative_score is not higher, or if any run ends in a trust crisis, blackout or dismissal (parent 0 of 5), or if Dignity or Health reach the low part of their range in more runs than the parent. Uninformative if the drive is misread (on/off wrong in more than 10% of decisions).
notes: Contrarian to the lab's balance-first and risk-first consensus (F1, F3, F7 parent), and cross-branch: the frame, risk marking and Energy order come from f7-three-skills-v1, the Grow story preference and key-project main action from f8-secure-growth-v1. Gate is feedback-based (the latest review's promotion outcome), not calendar-based; no numbers. The f8 evidence is n=4 and confounded with f8's other modes. Overlaps f7-delivery-stories-v1 in the first half-year (both push delivery), but the trigger differs (unconditional drive vs a visible fall) and the drive also drops the balance and C/D rules.
